prompt: A car is $30$ km from home at $1$ hour and $150$ km from home at $3$ hours. What is its average speed in km per hour?
hint: Average speed is an average rate of change, which is the SLOPE between two points on the trip.

hints.text: Average speed is an average rate of change, which is the SLOPE between two points on the trip.
The distance changed by $150 - 30 = 120$ km while the time changed by $3 - 1 = 2$ hours. Divide the first change by the second.
Dividing gives $120 \div 2 = 60$, so the average speed is $60$ km per hour.

explanation: Average rate of change is the change in distance divided by the change in time.
Between the two readings this is $(150 - 30) \div (3 - 1) = 120 \div 2$.
So the average speed is $60$ km per hour.

alternativeExplanations.title: As rise over run
steps: Plot (1, 30) and (3, 150). The rise is 120 and the run is 2.
Slope = 120/2 = 60 — the same slope formula from Algebra 1, wearing a new name.

alternativeExplanations.title: Average versus right now
steps: This 60 km/h is the AVERAGE over the whole two hours, like a trip summary.
The speedometer at one instant could read 40 or 90 — a limit is what finds that instant value.
